items.title: Teacher found dead in SMK Bau toilet, police rule out foul play
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 6 — A female teacher was found dead in the toilet of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Bau yesterday morning. Bau district police chief Supt Mohd Haide A Rahman said police were alerted to the incident at about 8.53 am before a team was immediately dispatched to the school. Mohd Haide said the victim was last seen by a colleague in the teachers’ room at about 8.15 am, shortly before she went to the toilet.

items.title: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel prices down five sen this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 and unsubsidised diesel have each decreased by five sen per litre from Aug 6 to Aug 12, 2026. For unsubsidised diesel, the retail price is now set at RM4.57 per litre, compared with RM4.62 previously. Meanwhile, subsidised fuel prices remain unchanged, with Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95) at RM1.99 per litre, Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) at RM2.10 per litre, the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) at RM2.05 per litre and the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) at RM2.15 per litre.

items.title: Wall Street's performance isn't so 'exceptional' on the global stage
items.summary: But from a global perspective, the performance of Wall Street – and the US – is far from exceptional. So far this year, the S&P 500 and Dow are up 12 per cent, and the Nasdaq is up 14 per cent. MIND THE GAP US earnings growth forecasts for the second quarter and calendar year 2026 are impressive.

items.title: DVS: Rocky the dog death probe referred to DPP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The investigation papers into the death of a dog in Klang, which recently sparked public attention, have been submitted to the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) for review. The Selangor Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) said the investigation papers were referred to the DPP's office yesterday together with several recommendations based on the findings of the probe. It said further action would be taken after receiving instructions from the DPP.

items.title: US refunds US$100bil in tariffs struck down by Supreme Court
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration has refunded about US$100 billion from tariffs that it collected before the US Supreme Court struck down those duties, a court filing showed. DETAILS: * The court filing in the US Court of International Trade said that "refunds (duties plus interest) of approximately US$100 billion have been completed using the Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries Refund component, certified by the agency, and sent to the U.S. Department of Treasury for disbursement." * It represented more than half of the US$166 billion collected in tariffs that the Supreme Court struck down in February.

items.title: Ringgit opens slightly higher as soft us data weighs on greenback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Thursday, supported by improved market sentiment after weaker-than-expected United States (US) economic data weighed on the greenback. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said softer-than-expected US economic data had pushed the US Dollar Index (DXY) down 0.18 per cent to 99.676. Mohd Afzanizam said US Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook had indicated she would support an interest rate hike if inflation remained persistently high.

items.title: Bukit Aman to send team to Jakarta to probe Malaysian pilot drug case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) will send a team of investigators and intelligence officers from Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (JSJN) to Jakarta, Indonesia next week to gather more information related to the syndicate network believed to be involved in a drug smuggling case involving a Malaysian pilot. Bukit Aman JSJN director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the team will be in Jakarta from Aug 11 to 15 to assist in completing the investigation, including identifying the source of drug supplies, smuggling methods, and the possibility of the suspects’ connections with syndicates in Indonesia. He said the investigation is important to identify the entire distribution chain, including the possibility of involvement of other parties.

items.title: Anwar meets Singapore GP chief ahead of Formula 1 return to Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday met Singapore Grand Prix (GP) Executive Director Michael Roche ahead of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) this October. Formula 1 and the FIA previously announced that the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix will be held at SIC from Oct 2 to 4 under a collaboration between Malaysia and Bahrain. The Bahrain Grand Prix was originally scheduled to take place at the Bahrain International Circuit in April but was postponed to October following geopolitical tensions in West Asia.

items.title: RM3.03bil Penang Mutiara LRT systems contract awarded to MRCB-Theta Edge JV
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Mass Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) has awarded the RM3.03 billion system turnkey contract for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project to a joint venture between Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) and Theta Edge Bhd. The award marks a key milestone in delivering Penang's first metro rail system, allowing railway systems design and integration to proceed alongside ongoing civil works. The contract covers seven core packages: rolling stock and depot equipment, signalling and train control, trackwork, power supply, railway supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA), telecommunications and information technology systems, and automatic fare collection.

items.title: Heritage building collapse raises safety concerns at Lebuh Armenian
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Shock and concern gripped traders and visitors in Lebuh Armenian after a heritage building facade collapsed on Tuesday, injuring two Sri Lankan tourists and raising questions about the safety of ageing structures in the Unesco World Heritage Site. The incident, which occurred about 1pm on one of Penang's busiest tourist streets, left business operators worried that public confidence could be shaken if similar incidents recur. [[nid:1505076]] She said the nearby Cheah Kongsi conducted inspections of its heritage building several times a year.

items.title: BN stays out of DAP's cabinet vote, calls it party matter
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional has described DAP's upcoming national congress, where delegates will vote on whether the party should remain in the unity government, as an internal party matter. BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir said it was up to DAP to decide its direction, dismissing suggestions that the vote reflected instability in the unity government. On calls for an early general election if DAP quits the government, Zambry said BN remained committed to political stability and continuity.

items.title: Salmonella outbreak linked to Mexican jalapenos sickens 345 across 27 US states
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US CDC and the FDA said on Wednesday they are investigating a multistate Salmonella outbreak linked to jalapeno peppers from Mexico, which have sickened 345 people across 27 states and prompted a recall of affected products. The FDA said 36 hospitalisations and no deaths have been reported, while the investigation remains ongoing. The US investigation identified restaurants including Chipotle Mexican Grill and QDOBA, a Mexican-style restaurant chain, as recipients of jalapenos imported by Coast Citrus Distributors.

items.title: DAP's Aug 16 vote a test of Anwar's unity government [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Political observers believe DAP's Aug 16 national congress will be a defining moment for the party and the unity government, as delegates will vote by secret ballot whether DAP should remain in the government until the end of the parliamentary term or withdraw. More than 4,000 delegates are expected to determine whether the party's ministers and deputy ministers should remain in the cabinet. DAP vice-chairman and Bangi MP Syahredzan Johan said the vote was essentially about whether DAP's ministers should remain in office, adding that the party would continue supporting Anwar as prime minister until the end of the parliamentary term.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI: Azeez says report did not mention his name
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has brushed aside Bersatu's call for him to confirm whether he had been contacted by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) over the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into the pilgrim fund. "The RCI report did not mention any of our names," he told the New Straits Times . Azeez was responding to Bersatu supreme council member Dr Afif Bahardin, who had urged Azeez to disclose a letter he claimed to possess from former MACC chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki, dated 2021, which purportedly cleared him of any wrongdoing in relation to the fund's management.

items.title: Drug arrests raise fears of syndicates recruiting Malaysians [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The recent arrests of Malaysians in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand over drug smuggling attempts could signal a broader recruitment drive by transnational drug syndicates targeting vulnerable Malaysians, said a crime watchdog. Malaysians Against Rape, Assault and Snatch Theft founder Dave Avran said the string of cases should not be viewed as isolated incidents but possible indicators of organised criminal networks exploiting Malaysians as disposable drug couriers. Increasingly, it looks like Malaysia is being mined for people willing to become the disposable workforce of international drug syndicates," he told the New Straits Times .

items.title: Myanmar president visits Thailand on quest for legitimacy as Bangkok backs engagement
items.summary: BANGKOK: Myanmar's junta chief turned President Min Aung Hlaing will make an official visit to Thailand on Thursday, as Bangkok makes a push for re-engagement between its war-torn neighbour and the regional bloc Asean. Thailand will be the fourth country Min Aung Hlaing has visited as president following official trips to China, India and Laos. Min Aung Hlaing as president has stressed his top priority is peace.

items.title: How a pilot who tested positive for drugs bypassed aviation's safety nets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: He was known within the industry as "a man with a temperament", yet met every technical requirement to fly a commercial aircraft. The case has exposed what industry insiders describe as a critical gap in aviation safety — a system focused on technical proficiency but with limited psychological screening and mental wellness safeguards. Speaking to the New Straits Times on condition of anonymity, a veteran pilot and industry insider said the pilot's temperament had been noted during his training and career progression, but the system was not designed to flag personality concerns as long as technical standards were met.

items.title: Pilot arrest puts KLIA, MAS security procedures under scrutiny
items.summary: They say Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd, airport security operators and aviation regulators must explain where the security chain broke down and whether screening and crew processing procedures were properly followed. Among key questions, he said, was whether the pilot underwent the prescribed crew screening process at KLIA, whether his baggage passed through the designated security lane or whether there was any opportunity to bypass standard procedures. Nik Huzlan also questioned whether the expedited processing of flight crew might have led to reduced vigilance.

items.title: US cyclosporiasis probe linked to lettuce widens to 15 states
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US health authorities have widened their probe into a cyclosporiasis outbreak tied to iceberg lettuce from central Mexico after detecting cases in six additional states, raising the total to 15 states, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said on Wednesday. The newly linked states are Missouri, Arkansas, Iowa, Nebraska, New Hampshire and North Carolina, the source said. The total case count associated with this multistate outbreak is now 6,358 illnesses reported from 15 states with at least 278 hospitalisations, CDC and FDA said.

items.title: Pilots' chief calls pilot's arrest a 'double embarrassment' for Malaysia Airlines [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Pilots Association is deeply embarrassed about the arrest of a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Indonesia for allegedly attempting to smuggle 25kg of ecstasy pills into the republic. Its president, Captain Ab Manan Mansor, said the involvement of a crew member from the national carrier was a "double embarrassment". He said Malaysia Airlines pilots typically reach the rank of captain, or four bars, by 30.

items.title: Faced with a teleprompter glitch, Canada's Carney mocks Trump
items.summary: TORONTO: When his teleprompter malfunctioned on Wednesday in the middle of a news conference on housing policy, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney smiled and took a swift jab at US President Donald Trump, saying, "I do not view this as a conspiracy." Carney's remark was an apparent reference to Trump's demands for an investigation after he encountered a halted escalator and a non-functioning teleprompter last year at the United Nations General Assembly, where he delivered a speech. Carney, who has said he would fight Trump's trade policies, has worked to lessen Canada's diplomatic and economic dependency on the US.

items.title: Court declares Seremban-born girl a Malaysian, rules anti-statelessness protection applies to her
items.summary: The Court of Appeal has ruled that the answer is “yes”, holding that such a child has been “abandoned” as a newborn. They also do not know who her birth mother is. The Court of Appeal decided that a child is still considered abandoned when a birth mother permanently disappears after intentionally giving up the child to a responsible adult or safe person.

items.title: Lorry skids near railway tracks: Shuttle Selatan, ETS service delayed
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU: Shuttle Selatan and Electric Train Service (ETS) operations on the Kulai–Kempas route were disrupted today after a lorry carrying flammable liquid skidded near the tracks, triggering a power outage. Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) said on Facebook that train operations were affected while cleanup work and repairs to restore the power supply were underway. "For affected ETS passengers, shuttle bus services will be provided at Kulai, Kempas Baru, and JB Sentral stations," KTMB said.

items.title: KL gazettes 9 more open spaces to protect green areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is stepping up efforts to safeguard Kuala Lumpur's green spaces by gazetting nine additional open areas. The nine newly gazetted open spaces include Lot 82448 in the Batu sub-district near Desa ParkCity Lake (6,607sq m); Lot 82443 in the Batu sub-district, also near Desa ParkCity Lake (22,000sq m); Lot 202030 in the Setapak sub-district, near Bayu Sentul Condominium (13,882sq m); and, Lot 38500 in the Petaling sub-district near Residensi Jalilmas (529sq m). Others are Lot 25119 in the Setapak sub-district, near Masjid Salahuddin Al-Ayubbi in Taman Melati (1,456sq m); Lot 39399 in the Petaling sub-district, near East Bukit Jalil Condominium (1,658 sq m); Lot 39397 in the Petaling sub-district, also near East Bukit Jalil Condominium (185sq m); Lot 56219 in the Batu sub-district, near United Point Mall (3,679sq m); and, Lot 482950 in the Kuala Lumpur sub-district, near Padang TURF Tasik Permaisuri (1,505sq m).

items.title: Penang to inspect all heritage buildings after wall collapse
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang will assess the structural safety of all heritage buildings after a wall collapsed in Lebuh Armenian on Tuesday, injuring two Sri Lankan tourists. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said the state government would ask the Heritage Department to conduct a study and appoint an independent engineer to identify unsafe buildings. The Sri Lankan tourists were injured when stones and timber from a first-floor beam of a heritage building fell on them.

items.title: US cooling firm to build US$150m plant in Nilai
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: US-based sustainable cooling solutions provider BAC will invest US$150 million to establish a new manufacturing plant in Nilai, Negri Sembilan. The Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) said the investment is expected to create up to 200 high-skilled jobs by 2035, including engineering and professional roles. Mida said the Nilai facility will house BAC's climate-controlled product development and testing laboratory in the Asia-Pacific region.

items.title: N. Korea warns of 'military options'
items.summary: SEOUL: The powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un yesterday accused Japan of "transformation into a war state" as Tokyo beefs up its military stance in the Pacific. In a statement carried by North Korean state media, Kim Yo-jong said Pyongyang's "leadership will set up additional military options which are obviously due to Japan's transformation". "Japan, a war criminal state, is accelerating its transformation into a war state," said her statement published by the Korean Central News Agency.

items.title: South Korea police raid Starbucks HQ over 'Tank Day' controversy
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korean police raided the Starbucks national headquarters Wednesday, the chain's local operator told AFP, following allegations an advertising campaign defamed activists slain in 1980 pro-democracy protests. A civic group and bereaved families filed a complaint accusing members of the Shinsegae Group, which operates Starbucks Korea, of defaming and insulting the victims and relatives. "The Seoul police raided the headquarters of Starbucks Korea this morning as part of the ongoing investigation," a Shinsegae Group spokesman told AFP, declining to provide further details.

items.title: Four men stabbed in London, woman arrested
items.summary: LONDON: A woman was arrested after four men were stabbed Wednesday in Covent Garden, a busy central London area popular with tourists, in a suspected "mental health related incident", police said. The 47-year-old woman was detained on suspicion of possessing an offensive weapon and assault following the stabbings shortly before 12.30pm local time (1130 GMT), according to London's Metropolitan Police. She remained in custody Wednesday afternoon, it said, noting officers had seized a pair of scissors at the scene.

items.title: Israel resumes Lebanon strikes amid Rome ceasefire talks
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel's military resumed strikes in southern Lebanon on Wednesday despite ongoing talks, blaming a ceasefire violation by Hizbollah as state media reported at least one person killed. The fresh strikes, accompanied by the first evacuation warning in weeks, came as the United States led diplomacy between Israel and Lebanon in Rome aimed at putting an end to hostilities, with Beirut seeking Israel's phased withdrawal from the south. "In response to a blatant violation of the ceasefire by the Hizbollah, the IDF has begun conducting precise strikes in southern Lebanon," the military said in a statement, shortly after telling residents to evacuate the town of Mansouri in the south.

items.title: Iran, Oman near Hormuz deal as US remains key obstacle
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran and Oman have agreed a route for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and are putting the final touches on arrangements for jointly managing the waterway, Teheran's foreign ministry said Wednesday. But official sources briefing Iranian media stressed that any reopening of the strait would depend on the United States fulfilling what Teheran sees as its commitment to end its own naval blockade of Iran's ports. Iran has seized de facto control of the strait, a strategic waterway for global energy trade, since the United States and Israel launched their war against the country on Feb 28.

items.title: Netanyahu: Israel did not agree to US-backed Gaza plan
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Israel did not agree to the US-backed plan for Gaza, even after receiving assurances that an Israeli pullout would only happen after Hamas disarms. The group's movement, meanwhile, reiterated its commitment to the roadmap published by US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace last week, which includes provisions for the group to hand over its weapons and an Israeli withdrawal. In a video posted to his social media accounts on Tuesday night, Netanyahu said Trump's team "believes that they can bring about the disarmament of Hamas and the demilitarisation of Gaza."

items.title: Progressive El-Sayed wins Michigan primary in jolt to Democrats
items.summary: DETROIT: The Democratic Party's progressive wing scored a high-profile victory when Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's US Senate primary, according to media projections on Wednesday, giving its anti-establishment message a boost ahead of November's midterm elections. He will face Republican former congressman Mike Rogers in November. Tuesday's vote, billed as a defining test of the party's direction, became an election-night cliffhanger, with El-Sayed notching a narrow victory over US Representative Haley Stevens, a moderate supported by Democratic leaders and pro-Israel groups.

items.title: India's Gen Z chooses protest over politics
items.summary: INDIA'S Gen Z Cockroach Janta Party, whose recent protest against exam paper leaks claimed a rare ministerial scalp, has no immediate plans to enter electoral politics, its founder said on Tuesday. Abhijeet Dipke spearheaded demonstrations that spread nationwide from Delhi, forcing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's education minister to resign, and spotlighting young people's worries about high jobless rates despite rapid economic growth. "In India, I don't think that forming a political party is a solution right now," Dipke added.

items.title: Iran's strategy is to outlast Washington
items.summary: IRAN is betting it can outlast Washington by turning the Middle East's trade routes, shipping lanes and energy infrastructure into pressure points that steadily raise the cost of confrontation, according to Gulf officials and analysts. Rather than seeking a decisive military victory, Teheran is pursuing a strategy of calibrated escalation aimed at widening the conflict without triggering full-scale war. The message from Teheran is that unless Washington accepts a new status quo that gives Iran a greater role in Hormuz, the conflict could spread beyond the Gulf.

items.title: Cabinet congratulates Malaysian contingent on Glasgow 2026 success, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — The Cabinet today congratulated the Malaysian contingent for its outstanding achievement at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, said Madani Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. “The Cabinet took the opportunity to congratulate the Malaysian contingent at the Commonwealth Games, whose success has made the country proud and brought honour to Malaysia. The contingent surpassed the target of five gold medals and recorded Malaysia’s best performance at the Commonwealth Games since winning 12 gold medals at the New Delhi 2010 edition.

items.title: State and district education offices to nominate schools for MOE reform initiative, each to get RM100,000, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR, Aug 5 — District Education Offices (PPDs) and State Education Departments (JPNs) are responsible for identifying and nominating schools to participate in the Ministry of Education’s (MOE) school reform programme, Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said. He said 10 high-performing schools in each district, comprising five primary and five secondary schools, will be selected based on their academic achievement, co-curricular performance, and student character development. Announced on July 27, the school reform programme encompasses comprehensive improvements in school work processes, teaching methods, mental health support, and the overall well-being of the school community.

items.title: At 76, Mustapa Mohamed rules out GE16 return, urges young leaders to take helm
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Aug 5 — Former Jeli Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Mustapa Mohamed has reaffirmed that he has no intention of contesting in the 16th General Election (GE16), saying it is time for a new generation of leaders to take on greater responsibilities. Mustapa, who rejoined Umno in June through the party’s Rumah Bangsa initiative, said the country’s changing political landscape and evolving voter expectations make it important to provide opportunities for younger leaders. Mustapa left Umno in September 2018 to join Bersatu before rejoining the party in June this year under the Rumah Bangsa initiative.

items.title: Finance Ministry urges public not to spread false poster on RM100 SARA payout for National Day
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) today denied a viral claim that all Malaysians aged 18 and above will receive a one-off RM100 Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) payment in conjunction with National Day. In a social media post, MOF said the poster making the claim was false. The ministry advised the public not to believe or share the poster.

items.title: MACC questions former CFO for six hours over Tabung Haji RCI findings
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — A former chief financial officer (CFO) of a statutory body-owned company spent more than six hours giving a statement to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today to assist in the investigation regarding findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on Tabung Haji. The statement recording session, which took place at the MACC Headquarters here, began at around 10.30am and concluded at approximately 5pm today. Meanwhile, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said in a statement today said that it was the second day of recording statements from the former senior official after he was released yesterday.

items.title: Fahmi: Social media platforms given time to align with ONSA on scams, online gambling
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — Social media platform operators have been given time to align their internal mechanisms to ensure that the removal of high-risk content involving scams and online gambling is carried out automatically. These two codes will be used to ensure that platforms comply with regulations related to online safety, including content involving scams and online gambling. Fahmi, who is also the Madani government spokesman, said the requirement for the automatic removal of harmful content is important as the number of takedown requests made by MCMC, particularly involving online gambling and scam-related content, has exceeded last year’s total.

items.title: Police submit Rocky dog death probe in Klang to DPP, owner weighing legal options
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Police have submitted the investigation paper on the death of Rocky the dog to the deputy public prosecutor’s office. South Klang police chief Asst Comm Lim Jit Huey said the paper was handed over yesterday, The Star reported. “The investigation paper on Rocky was referred to the DPP yesterday.

items.title: Man suffers burns in fire that damaged five RAKR houses in Seberang Jerteh
items.summary: Jertih Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) Chief Mustafa Ismail said his team received an emergency call at 10.28am and arrived at the location at 11.44am, before successfully controlling the fire about 30 minutes later. “The fire involved five permanent residential houses, with one house completely destroyed and another almost completely destroyed, while the other three suffered damages ranging between 5 and 50 per cent,” he said. “A total of 14 firefighters and personnel along with two fire engines from the Jertih and Besut fire stations were involved in the firefighting operation, which utilised water from a nearby fire hydrant.

items.title: Fahmi: PKR congress to assess party performance in Johor, Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The upcoming PKR national congress is expected to look into the party’s performance in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections and also the federal government’s policies, said PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. “Delegates, especially from Johor and Negeri Sembilan, are expected to share their views and experiences to identify weaknesses and propose improvements for the party. He said that the congress is also likely to see proposals from delegates regarding improvements to government policies.

items.title: PM directs Human Resources Ministry to expedite 15,000 foreign worker applications, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) to immediately process the first 15,000 foreign worker applications to address labour shortages in key sectors and support Malaysia’s economic activities. Communications Minister and Madani Government spokesperson Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the move was aimed at meeting workforce demand across affected industries. Prior to this, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan announced that Kesuma had assumed full responsibility for managing the One-Stop Centre (OSC) for Foreign Worker Management with immediate effect, following a Cabinet decision on July 1.

items.title: Penang Second Bridge eastbound route to Batu Kawan closed Aug 8 night for Cultural Night Run
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 5 — The eastbound route on the Sultan Abdul Halim Mu’adzam Shah Bridge (JSAHMS), from Batu Maung to Batu Kawan, will be temporarily closed from 8pm on August 8 until 3am on August 9. However, the westbound route from Batu Kawan to Batu Maung will remain open, as will routes from Bandar Cassia and the Batu Kawan Industrial Park (BKIP) to the North-South Expressway (PLUS). JKSB advised motorists travelling from Penang island to the mainland during the closure to use the Penang Bridge.

items.title: Works minister: LPT2 concessionaire to repair fence, review long‑term safety after elephant crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The concessionaire of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2) has been instructed to immediately repair the damaged safety fence and review long-term measures to enhance safety following a collision involving a vehicle and a herd of elephants at KM274.6 northbound along the Cheneh-Chukai stretch last night. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said an inspection at the site found that the existing safety fence had collapsed, believed to have been damaged after being struck by the herd of elephants passing through the area. As an initial preventive measure, he said the LPT2 concessionaire has also been instructed to increase the frequency of patrols, particularly at night, in high-risk areas to monitor wildlife movement and ensure the safety of highway users.

items.title: Immigration busts passport forgery syndicate in KL raids, arrests three, seizes 119 forged passports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) detained three Indonesian nationals, including a man suspected to be the mastermind of a passport forgery syndicate, during operations at two locations around here last night. Its director-general, Datuk Zakaria Shaaban, said that three individuals involved, namely two men and one woman aged between 30 and 50, were detained during operations at 11 pm in Taman Sri Kuching and Taman Bukit Cheras, here. He also suspected that the syndicate mastermind is believed to have committed an offence under Section 12(1)(f) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while two other foreign nationals are believed to have committed offences under Section 6(1)© of the Immigration Act 1959/63.

items.title: Defence minister on two‑day visit to Hanoi to strengthen Malaysia‑Vietnam defence ties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin began a two-day official visit to Vietnam today to strengthen defence cooperation between the two countries. He said the visit marks his first official trip to Vietnam since being appointed Defence Minister. “Malaysia and Vietnam have long enjoyed close defence ties.

items.title: Malaysia to discuss refugee repatriation plan with Myanmar junta, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The Malaysian government will hold talks with the Myanmar junta over the proposed repatriation of 5,000 refugees to the country, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said the Myanmar junta must also ensure that the refugees would not face any danger before the repatriation process could begin. On July 29, it was reported that the Myanmar junta had agreed to receive 5,000 Myanmar refugees from Malaysia.

items.title: Fahmi: Up to 40 MPs ready to debate Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said up to 40 parliamentarians have expressed their willingness to debate the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the Tabung Haji (TH) board at the Dewan Rakyat special sitting next week. He said the Cabinet was also informed that Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul had agreed for the special sitting to be held continuously without a break. Fahmi, who is also the unity government spokesman, said the public could follow the Dewan Rakyat special sitting through live broadcasts on all official media channels.

items.title: Fahmi says tighter airport security measures being considered after pilot’s arrest over alleged drug trafficking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The government is considering several security measures to be implemented at airports following the recent arrest of a Malaysian pilot in Indonesia over alleged drug trafficking, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said more stringent aviation security measures, in addition to tighter screening protocols, were among the measures being considered. “This would involve deploying regular police personnel together with Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB) Aviation Security (AVSEC) auxiliary police unit.

items.title: Federal police open five investigation papers over alleged Tabung Haji commercial crimes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Police have opened five investigation papers after receiving nine reports from Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), its subsidiary and members of the public over alleged commercial crimes, including matters raised in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH. Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said investigators were recording statements from witnesses in Malaysia and abroad, while obtaining relevant documents to complete the investigations. “Police are committed to ensuring that every investigation is conducted independently, transparently, professionally and in accordance with the law.

items.title: Johor police bust drug syndicate using vape cartridges, seize RM10.68m worth of drugs
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 5 — Police have busted a drug trafficking syndicate that used vape cartridges to distribute drugs following the seizure of various types of drugs worth RM10.68 million in an operation across Johor on Aug 2. Johor deputy police chief DCP Hoo Chuan Huat said the operation, which began at 11 am, was carried out at five separate locations in Johor Bahru, Kulai and Muar, and led to the arrest of five local men, one foreign man and one foreign woman, aged between 36 and 46. Police also seized 47 plastic bottles containing vape liquid, a glass bottle containing 127.55 litres of methamphetamine liquid, two plastic packets believed to contain cocaine, one plastic packet containing ketamine, and a vape liquid filling machine.

items.title: MOH upgrading health facilities in Sabah, Sarawak interior based on local needs, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — The Health Ministry (MOH) is adopting a tailored approach to upgrading health facilities in the interior of Sabah and Sarawak by taking into account the geographical challenges and specific needs of each area, said Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib. Through the Borneo Health Tour, she said the ministry found that each health clinic visited had its own specific needs, whether in terms of additional equipment, more personnel, expanded space or relocation from less suitable sites. “Every health clinic I have visited faces different constraints.

items.title: Deputy minister: Security laws must protect safety without undermining human rights
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 5 — Efforts to strengthen national security must not come at the expense of human rights, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department for Law and Institutional Reform M. Kulasegaran said. He said both priorities must advance together through an effective, balanced and forward-looking legal framework. “Legal reform had become increasingly important as technology, society and security threats continued to evolve.

items.title: MACC remands three more over alleged RM450,000 misuse of penalty payments
items.summary: Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah issued the remand order until Aug 9 against the three men, who are in their 50s, following an application by the MACC at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court today. According to a MACC source, the three were arrested at the commission’s headquarters at about 6 pm yesterday. Meanwhile, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests and said the case was being investigated under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: High Court acquits temple chairman over alleged trespass at Sri Maha Mariamman temple
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — The High Court today acquitted a temple chairman who had been charged with trespassing at the Sri Maha Mariamman Temple on privately owned land last year, Sinar Harian reported. Lawyer Latheefa Koya, who represented M Paramaguru, 49, said Justice Hazlina Hussain quashed the charge after finding it was fatally defective. In a statement, Latheefa said the court ruled the charge failed to disclose the criminal intent required to constitute the offence of trespass.

items.title: Selangor AI White Paper to outline landscape, map benefits, challenges, value proposition, says MB
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 5 — The Selangor government’s artificial intelligence (AI) White Paper, which is currently being developed, will outline the overall landscape for the use of the technology, including its challenges, benefits and value proposition. “The AI White Paper will serve as a guideline for us, particularly in Selangor, on how we should approach, live with and interact with AI,” he said. Amirudin said the AI White Paper would be tabled at the State Legislative Assembly for debate at a later date.

items.title: Cops investigate housebreaking, robbery in Tanjung Bungah; CCTV shows lone suspect in five‑day crime spree
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 5 — Police have opened investigation papers into four crimes reported in Tanjung Bungah between July 28 and August 2, involving housebreaking, robbery, trespassing and theft. Northeast district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said two of the four cases resulted in losses estimated at about RM17,000, while the other two caused no losses, refuting claims circulating on social media that five incidents had occurred in the area. He said police believed a man wearing a red shirt seen in CCTV footage could be linked to some of the incidents, although investigations were ongoing to establish the connection.
